brief.headline: Memory in bear mode despite deal flow: hyperscaler capex hits $690B, CoWoS easing, but pricing power intact through Q3
brief.summary: <cite index="43-1,43-7">Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix are all down more than 20% from recent closing highs, entering bear-market territory despite Samsung's record profit guidance of $59 billion operating profit.</cite> <cite index="40-1,40-2">Both Samsung and SK Hynix are set to unveil major long-term memory chip supply deals with leading US technology companies during President Lee's Silicon Valley visit.</cite> <cite index="19-2,19-6">The five largest US hyperscalers have collectively committed to spending between $660 billion and $690 billion on capital expenditure in 2026, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with the vast majority directed at AI compute and data centers.</cite> <cite index="28-2,28-11">TSMC's monthly CoWoS capacity could reach a record 120,000 to 140,000 wafers in 2026, with the supply-demand gap narrowing from around 20% currently to about 10% by the end of 2026.</cite> <cite index="16-1,16-2">DRAM contract prices are projected to rise another 13%-18% in Q3 2026, while NAND Flash contract prices are expected to increase 10%-15% QoQ.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%.</cite> <cite index="5-3">Channel checks indicate SK Hynix will likely secure a largely stable market share in the HBM market in 2026 around 50% of total bits.</cite> <cite index="39-11,39-12">SK Hynix plans to invest 100 trillion won ($64.37 billion) in South Korea, with construction of its M17 NAND fabrication plant set to begin next year and operations targeted for the first half of 2029.</cite> Stay long SK Hynix vs. Samsung. SK Hynix maintains HBM qualification lead with ~50% market share vs. Samsung's delayed HBM3E qualification struggles. Near-term Samsung beat likely priced; SK's capex cycle and NAND pivot (M17 fab 1H29 online) positions better for 2027-28 enterprise SSD wave. Watch Friday's US listing for SK Hynix as sentiment test.

memory_cycle.stage: Late-stage boom with consumer demand destruction
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="17-10">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% quarter over quarter in Q1 2026.</cite> <cite index="8-3,8-13">The top three memory makers have already allocated their full HBM output for the year, with Micron guiding for a 68% gross margin in the second quarter of 2026.</cite> <cite index="11-1">Conventional DRAM contract prices are projected to rise 13% to 18% QoQ in Q3 2026, with NAND Flash contract prices increasing 10% to 15%, a marked slowdown from Q1 record gains.</cite> <cite index="11-9,11-10">Demand for AI inference systems and hyperscale data centers remains strong enough to keep both DRAM and NAND supply constrained, while memory manufacturers continue shifting production capacity toward higher-margin server products, leaving less capacity available for consumer memory.</cite> Supply discipline holding; ASP deceleration not collapse.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,5-6">HBM bit shipments are projected to jump 35% next year to 17.1 billion gigabits, with TSMC's latest call showing AI demand is running well ahead of earlier forecasts.</cite> <cite index="8-8,8-9">SK hynix has emerged as the primary beneficiary, claiming to be the only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-generation HBM4 at scale.</cite> <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only a 'minimal to modest downtick' in HBM3E pricing for 2026 compared with 2025 as more suppliers come online.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-2">Investors and analysts expect memory shortages to last through 2027, which could give the leading suppliers stronger pricing power than the industry has usually enjoyed.</cite> HBM3E remains sold out; Samsung qualification noise creating tactical pricing pushback from Nvidia but structurally irrelevant through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix to unveil major chip supply deals during Lee's Silicon Valley visit
news_pulse.implication: Long-term memory chip supply deals with leading US tech firms signal continued hyperscaler demand visibility; potential for multi-year LTAs to lock in pricing and volumes through 2027-28.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex guidance for 2026 reaches $690B, up 81% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B confirms AI infrastructure buildout accelerating; ~75% ($450B) directly tied to AI servers, GPUs, datacenters.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS capacity reaching 120-140K wafers/month in 2026 (vs. 75-80K end-2025) eases HBM packaging bottleneck; structurally positive for memory attach rates but reduces premium Nvidia could extract from packaging scarcity.

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks enter bear market: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron down >20% from highs
news_pulse.implication: Samsung's record $59B operating profit estimate failed to impress; sector lost $1.5T market cap since June 25. Cyclicality fears resurfacing despite structural AI demand thesis. Tactical reset, not fundamental break.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 2026 DRAM pricing to rise 13-18% QoQ, NAND 10-15%: TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: Deceleration from Q1's 93-98% DRAM spike signals pricing power intact but normalizing. NAND rising faster than DRAM for first time this cycle due to enterprise SSD demand from AI deployments.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64.4B) South Korea investment plan
news_pulse.implication: M17 NAND fab (80 trillion won) construction begins 2027, operations 1H 2029; P&T7 advanced packaging facility (20 trillion won) expansion targets HBM servers and DRAM. Signals conviction in multi-year AI memory supercycle.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix held 57% global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025 vs. Samsung 22%, Micron 21%
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix's dominant HBM position reflects early HBM3E qualification and Nvidia design wins. Samsung's qualification delays and reported pricing pushback create near-term share risk but 2027+ supply additions could shift dynamics.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia secures 60% of global CoWoS capacity for 2025-2026
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia booking 595K CoWoS wafers by 2026 (515K from TSMC, 80K from Amkor/ASE) for Rubin, Vera, GB100. Limits AMD/Broadcom/others to 40% of capacity; competitive moat remains intact through 2027 despite capacity adds.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures likely range-bound near-term ahead of earnings. Memory sector volatility elevated; leveraged retail positioning in SK Hynix warrants caution on further downside if selloff extends. Watch ADR-KRX arb for overnight gaps.
